questions.problem:
The matrix $E$ and the vector $b$ are given below.
Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(E).$ 
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}\cdot {x}_{4}$, where ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$, ${x}_{3}$, and ${x}_{4}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{e}_{1}+{x}_{2}{e}_{2}+{x}_{3}{e}_{3}+{x}_{4}{e}_{4},$ and ${e}_{1}$, ${e}_{2}$, ${e}_{3}$, and ${e}_{4}$ are respective columns of $E.$

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}8 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ 16 & -4 & 10 & 2 \\ 11 & -3 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(E),$ we need to check if the equation $Ex=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[E\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[E\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -2 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 16 & -4 & 10 & 2 & -1 \\ 11 & -3 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}8 & -2 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -9 \\ 11 & -3 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}8{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}+{x}_{4}=4 \\ 0=-9 \\ 11{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-{x}_{4}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get a false statement $0=-9.$ Therefore, the system is inconsistent, and we conclude that $b\notin \text{Col}(E).$

questions.problem: Consider the matrix given by $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 \\ -2 & -11 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}14 \\ -15 \\ k+5\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(A).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(A),$ then the equation $Ax=b$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 14 \\ -2 & -11 & -15 \\ 1 & 6 & k+5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & k+5 \\ -2 & -11 & -15 \\ 3 & 8 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & k+5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2k-5 \\ 3 & 8 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & k+5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2k-5 \\ 0 & -10 & -3k-1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+10{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & k+5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2k-5 \\ 0 & 0 & 17k-51\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=k+5 \\ {x}_{2}=2k-5 \\ 0=17k-51.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=17k-51,$ which means that $k=3.$

questions.problem:
The matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are given below.
Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(A).$ 
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3},$ and ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, and ${a}_{3}$ are the respective columns of $A.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -8 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(A),$ we need to check if the equation $Ax=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -8 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -8 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & -6 & 12 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-6){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -8 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -12 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-8{x}_{3}=-2 \\ -{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=2 \\ -12{x}_{3}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting it into the second equation gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2}+4(\frac{1}{2}) & =2 \\ -{x}_{2}+2 & =2 \\ {x}_{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, from the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3(0)-8(\frac{1}{2}) & =-2 \\ {x}_{1}-4 & =-2 \\ {x}_{1} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we have a solution, the equation $Ax=b$ is consistent, which implies that $b\in \text{Col}(A).$ 

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1},$ ${a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}=2\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+0\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}
$$

Finally, we get ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=2\cdot 0\cdot \frac{1}{2}=0.$

questions.problem: Consider the matrix given by $A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ k \\ 10\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(A).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(A),$ then the equation $Ax=b$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & -8 \\ 0 & -3 & k \\ 1 & 1 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 10 \\ 0 & -3 & k \\ -5 & 1 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 10 \\ 0 & -3 & k \\ 0 & 6 & 42\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 10 \\ 0 & -3 & k \\ 0 & 0 & 42+2k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=10 \\ -3{x}_{2}=k \\ 0=42+2k.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=42+2k,$ which means that $k=-21.$
